anchor_definition: The anchor is the encode-pipeline ENTRY l = function(t){return a(c(o(t)))}: the shallowest function that represents 'the encoding' as a whole, composing the inner stages o -> c -> a. Graded below it along the encode path: a (final stage that maps index pairs onto the 24-char socialist-values alphabet h, the target-specific output binding) 0.7; c (the base-12 conversion that is the core encoding algorithm) 0.5; o (the string->hex preprocessing via encodeURIComponent) 0.2; e (the generic assert/varargs helper c calls) 0.1. Off-chain (0): the inverse decode entry s and its decode-only helpers f (array->hex) and u (hex->string).

anchor.why: The encode entry: composes o, c and a to turn the raw input string into the final encoded output string assigned to the output textarea (p.value = l(v.value)).

roles.why: The final pipeline stage a=function(t){return t.map(t=>h[2*t]+h[2*t+1]).join('')}: maps index pairs onto the 24-char alphabet h (富强民主...), binding the output to THIS encoder's socialist-values characters. The target-specific output stage nested below the entry.

The core encoding transform c=function(t){...Number.parseInt(a,16)...push base-12 indices with 10/11 markers...}: converts the hex string into the index array a() consumes. The reusable base-conversion algorithm at the heart of the encode.

The first stage o=function(t){...encodeURIComponent(r).replace(/%/g,'').toUpperCase()}: turns the raw input into the uppercase hex string c() consumes. A path-critical preprocessing step, but a generic string->hex transform.
A generic assert/varargs helper e=function(){...throw new Error(...)} that c calls to validate its argument. A low-level generic helper on the upstream path.
The inverse DECODE entry s=function(t){...h.indexOf(s)...f(n)...u(v)...}: reads the alphabet back to bytes. Opposite direction; not on the encode path.
A decode-only helper f=function(t){...toString(16).toUpperCase()...}: array->hex, used by the decode entry s, not on the encode path. A sibling decoy.
A decode-only helper u=function(t){...decodeURIComponent(...)}: hex->string, used by the decode entry s, not on the encode path. A sibling decoy.
